# Sirach Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** All wisdom comes from the Lord, and with him it endures forever.

**2** The sands of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity — who can count them?

**3** The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depths of the abyss — who can search them out?

**4** Wisdom was created before all other things, and prudent understanding from the beginning.

**5** The source of wisdom is the word of God in the heights, and her courses are the everlasting commandments.

**6** To whom has the root of wisdom been disclosed? Who has known her subtle plans?

**7** To whom has the discipline of wisdom been revealed? Who has understood the abundance of her experience?

**8** There is one who is wise, the awe-inspiring one seated on his throne — the Lord.

**9** It is he who created her; he saw her and measured her, and poured her out upon all his works.

**10** She dwells with all flesh according to his bounty, and he lavished her upon those who love him.

**11** The fear of the Lord is honor and glory, delight and a festive crown.

**12** The fear of the Lord gladdens the heart, bringing happiness and joy and long life.

**13** For those who fear the Lord, all will be well at the last; on the day of their death they will be blessed.

**14** The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord; her branches are long life.

**15** Wisdom built her house among the people as an eternal foundation, and she will be entrusted to their offspring.

**16** To be filled with wisdom is to fear the Lord; she inebriates them with her fruits.

**17** She fills their whole house with choice things, and their storehouses with her harvest.

**18** The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, making peace and wholesome health to flourish.

**19** He rained down knowledge and sound understanding, and he glorified those who cling to her.

**20** To fear the Lord is the root of wisdom; her branches are long life.

**21** The fear of the Lord drives out sin; where it is present, it averts anger.

**22** A wrathful person cannot be justified, for the anger that is his undoing will prove his ruin.

**23** A patient person will hold on until the proper moment, and afterward joy will break out for him.

**24** Until the right time he will restrain his words, and the lips of many will declare his wisdom.

**25** In the treasury of wisdom are wise sayings, but to the sinner, piety is an abomination.

**26** If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will grant her to you freely.

**27** For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction; faithfulness and humility are his delight.

**28** Do not disobey the fear of the Lord; do not approach him with a divided heart.

**29** Do not be a hypocrite before others; keep watch over your lips.

**30** Do not exalt yourself lest you fall and bring disgrace upon your soul. The Lord will expose your secrets and bring you low in the assembly, because you did not approach the fear of the Lord, and your heart was full of deceit.
